concerns.concern: Using the authors' own Arrhenius parameters (76 and 236 meV), both proposed processes, PNR flipping and oxygen-vacancy ionization, would be completely frozen at the 1.4–10 K temperatures where the memory is written and erased. The ~1 kV/cm gate field is far too weak to lower those barriers meaningfully.
concerns.quote: both proposed processes (PNR flipping and OV ionization) would be thermally frozen at the 1.4–10 K temperatures where the memory is written and erased.

concerns.concern: The paper says the illumination-induced drop in Tc contradicts the expected trend. Its own data show Tc anticorrelated with mobility, so lower Tc with higher μ after illumination is what that correlation predicts. The proposed PNR–superconductivity link is therefore not distinguished from a simple Tc–disorder relation.
concerns.quote: The proposed PNR–superconductivity link is therefore not distinguished from a simple Tc–disorder correlation.

concerns.concern: The dark-relaxation time τ changes by only about a factor of two between 10 and 180 K. Thermally activated processes with 76 and 236 meV barriers would change it by many orders of magnitude.
concerns.quote: The relaxation time τ varies by only a factor of ~2 over 10–180 K, which is hard to reconcile with activation barriers of 76 and 236 meV.

concerns.concern: The dielectric loss-peak temperatures depend strongly on frequency. Extrapolated to the much slower time scales of gate cycling and dark relaxation, the peaks fall near 24 K and 73 K or lower. The matching of 35 K and 95 K across measurements therefore rests on an unstated choice of frequency.
concerns.quote: The matching of 35 K and 95 K across Fig. 3b, Fig. 3d and Fig. 4 therefore depends on an unstated choice of frequency.

concerns.concern: At 95 K the relaxation time in Fig. 4c is the largest in the data set, not a minimum as the text claims. This contradicts the idea that relaxation is accelerated there by thermally activated ionization.
concerns.quote: At 95 K, τ in Fig. 4c is a maximum, not the minimum claimed in the text.

concerns.concern: The claim that illumination completely erases the memory is never checked against the pristine, never-gated state. Because illumination also photodopes the sample, the illuminated state may be a distinct state rather than an erased one.
concerns.quote: 'Complete erasure' is asserted without comparing to the pristine state.

concerns.concern: The dark-relaxation magnitude in Fig. 4 (about a 14% rise in Rs) is several times larger than the illumination-induced drop. This conflicts with Supp. Fig. 5, where the same relaxation is only a fraction of that drop, so the normalization is unclear or the datasets disagree.
concerns.quote: Either the normalization in Fig. 4 is not ΔR/R1 as labelled, or the two figures come from different data with different behaviour.

concerns.concern: Because the LED characteristic depends on temperature, the photon dose varies uncontrolled across temperatures. This could create or distort the features at 35 K and 95 K. The optical power at the sample and saturation of Rs at each temperature are not reported, and the description of how the LED was driven is inconsistent.
concerns.quote: making it difficult to keep a constant illuminating flux at varying temperature

concerns.concern: Assigning loss Peak 2 to oxygen-vacancy charge states rests only on an energy match. Maxwell–Wagner interfacial polarization in the metal/insulator/2DEG stack could produce a similar Arrhenius peak.
concerns.quote: 2 is associated with OVs’ charge state

concerns.concern: A photon energy larger than the activation barriers does not show that light can drive PNR reorientation or OV charge changes. That requires a specific optical transition with nonzero cross-section.
concerns.quote: much smaller than the photon energy of 1.97 eV, and therefore can be activated by red light

concerns.concern: The claim that optical activation works even at extremely low temperatures is contradicted by Fig. 2b. There, illumination produces no obvious Rs change at 2 K.
concerns.quote: no obvious Rs change occurs under illumination at 2 K, apart from heating artifacts

concerns.concern: The asymmetric gate-current hysteresis cited to explain the initial drift after cooldown was measured on an illuminated, photodoped sample at 10 K, starting with a positive sweep. It may therefore reflect the return of photo-pumped electrons rather than the mechanism behind the pristine drift.
concerns.quote: After the sample is fully illuminated at 10 K, the first gate cycle generates a remarkable asymmetric

concerns.concern: The τ fits are fragile. At 10–25 K ΔR/R1 is nearly zero, so τ is undefined. The fitted τ values are comparable to the observation window, the 95 K trace is noisy, and no error bars are given.
concerns.quote: At 10–25 K, ΔR/R1 ≈ 0, so τ is essentially undefined.

concerns.concern: The dielectric measurement averages over the whole 0.5 mm substrate. It therefore does not specifically probe the interfacial region that couples to the 2DEG.
concerns.quote: The dielectric response is also an average over the full 0.5 mm substrate

concerns.concern: Leakage current is not separated from displacement current in the gate-current data.
concerns.quote: In addition, leakage current is not separated from displacement current.

concerns.concern: The small Hall-derived changes in n and μ are assembled from three separate runs of a strongly history-dependent system. Run-to-run reproducibility at the percent level is not shown, yet it is needed to trust the Type A vs Type B mobility difference.
concerns.quote: Run-to-run reproducibility at the percent level must therefore be demonstrated before the Type A vs. Type B difference in μ can be trusted.

concerns.concern: Key gate-protocol parameters are missing, such as the gate sweep rate and the holding times in the main experiments.
concerns.quote: Key protocol parameters are also missing: gate sweep rate, holding times in the main experiments

concerns.concern: It is not shown that the Hall response is linear up to ±6 T. Linearity is needed to justify a single-band extraction of carrier density.
concerns.quote: whether the Hall response at ±6 T is linear (single-band)

concerns.concern: The novelty is overstated. Gate-cycling enhancement of Tc and its link to polar lattice degrees of freedom were already reported in the cited ref. 30, so only the optical reset and the dielectric correlation appear new.
concerns.quote: a previously unrecognized interplay between the superconducting interface and emergent lattice excitations

concerns.concern: Supplementary Note 4 assigns the elevated resistance of 856 Ω·sq⁻¹ to the baseline symbol R_s^b. Its notation also differs from the main text, which risks confusion.
concerns.quote: leading to a higher sheet resistance
